I am not a major historian, but I have got an impression of what happened from what I've read. As a note this is all off the top of my head, as I certainly don't have the energy to go doing a lot of research right now.

A lot of things that went pretty wrong for a very long time, including incompetent and grossly corrupt leadership, frequent attacks that were not countered effectively, a politically indifferent/powerless population, and probably a lack of payment to the military (IIRC one standard form of payment was land that was conquered, hence one reason why they conquered so much, but there's only so much worthwhile land). The Byzantium managed to jettison most of their regional problems by jettisoning the western empire, allowing them to concentrate their entire resource pool on the eastern empire and to leave the west to collapse on itself. A decent number of people went there from Rome as well, which meant that a lot of people who would be able to help, e.g. skilled workers, scholars, and so forth, were no longer in the Western half, causing everything to sink that much faster.

People try to compare the US's current troubles to the Roman Empire, and while there are some similarities, it was a very different situation in a very different time and things persisted for probably upwards of two centuries and it just kept building on itself.

From what I have read, the Roman Empire fell from a combination of factors including:

-A government that responded to food shortages by attempting to set price controls, which killed the economy.

-The overuse of disloyal foreign mercenaries who only wanted to get paid, and turned against Rome when they were not.

-Increasing lawlessness, plagues and previously mentioned food prices which drove a mass depopulation of once great cities.

-Foreign invasion/migration by tribes which resettled in the bowels of the weakened empire and did not respect its authority.
